aa-30-en: Should training for the apostolate begin with children's earliest education and continue to be perfected throughout life?
aa-31-en: Do various forms of the apostolate require a specially suitable formation of the laity, including careful doctrinal preparation for evangelizing and sanctifying others?
aa-32-en: Are study sessions, congresses, spiritual exercises, meetings, books, and similar means offered as aids so lay persons can deepen Scripture, doctrine, and apostolic methods?
aa-33-en: Are all the laity earnestly invited to answer gladly and promptly Christ's more urgent invitation and the impulse of the Holy Spirit in this hour?
ag-1-en: Is the Church, as a universal sacrament of salvation, bound by her catholicity and her Founder's mandate to strive always to proclaim the Gospel to all people?
ag-2-en: Is the pilgrim Church missionary by her very nature, drawing her origin from the mission of the Son and of the Holy Spirit according to the Father's decree?
ag-3-en: Is God's universal design for salvation carried out not only secretly in the soul or by human religious seeking, but by His new intervention in history through sending His Son?
ag-4-en: Did Christ send the Holy Spirit from the Father to carry on inwardly His saving work and to prompt the Church to spread out among the nations?
ag-5-en: Did the Lord Jesus from the beginning call the Twelve to be with Him and to be sent out preaching, so that the Apostles were the beginning of the sacred hierarchy?
ag-6-en: Is the bishops' missionary duty, under Peter's successor and with the whole Church's help, one and the same everywhere, though carried out differently according to circumstances?
ag-7-en: Does missionary activity arise from God's will that all be saved and come to the knowledge of the truth, so that all must be converted to Christ and incorporated into Him by baptism?
ag-8-en: Is missionary activity closely bound up with human nature and its aspirations, inasmuch as by manifesting Christ the Church reveals the real truth about the human condition?
ag-9-en: Does the time for missionary activity extend between the Lord's first and second coming, so that the Gospel must be preached to all nations before He comes?
ag-10-en: Is the Church, sent to reveal and communicate God's love to all, still faced with a gigantic missionary task among peoples who have scarcely heard the Gospel?
ag-11-en: Must the Church be present among unevangelized peoples through her children, who by life and word show forth the new man of baptism and the power of the Holy Spirit?
ag-12-en: Should the presence of Christians among human groups be inspired by that charity with which God has loved us, extending without distinction of race, creed, or social condition?
ag-13-en: Wherever God opens a door for proclaiming Christ's mystery, should the living God and Jesus Christ sent for the salvation of all be announced to all with confidence and constancy?
ag-14-en: Is the catechumenate not a mere expounding of doctrines but a training in the whole Christian life, joining disciples to Christ by instruction and successive sacred rites?
ag-15-en: Does the Holy Spirit, calling all to Christ through the Gospel, gather those who believe into the one People of God, so that missionaries should raise up congregations of the faithful?
ag-16-en: Does the Church take deeper root among a people when local communities have their own bishops, priests, and deacons from among their members?
ag-17-en: Are men and women catechists, imbued with the apostolic spirit, of great importance for missionary work, so that their training must be carefully adapted to cultural advances?
ag-18-en: Should religious life be carefully fostered from the planting stage of the Church, both as aid to missions and as a sign of the inner nature of the Christian calling?
ag-19-en: Does the planting of the Church reach a certain goal when a locally rooted congregation of the faithful has firm stability, local clergy, and the ministries needed under its own bishop?
ag-20-en: Is a particular church bound to represent the universal Church as perfectly as possible, and thus also sent to those in its territory who do not yet believe in Christ?
ag-21-en: Has a church not been really founded or fully alive as a perfect sign of Christ unless a laity worthy of the name works along with the hierarchy?
ag-22-en: In harmony with the Incarnation, should young churches rooted in Christ take to themselves the riches of their peoples' customs, wisdom, and traditions?
ag-23-en: Although every disciple must spread the Faith, does Christ also specially call some and raise up institutes whose special task is preaching to the nations?
ag-24-en: Must one who is called respond to God without taking counsel with flesh and blood, devoted wholly to the Gospel and ready to remain in that vocation for life?
ag-25-en: Must the future missionary be prepared by special spiritual and moral training for initiative, perseverance, patience in hardship, and adaptation to foreign ways of life?
ag-26-en: Should those sent to the nations be nourished with the words of faith and good doctrine, drawn principally from Sacred Scripture and the mystery of Christ?
ag-27-en: Since mission work can scarcely be done by lone individuals, are missionaries rightly gathered into institutes trained and directed under the hierarchy in the Church's name?
ag-28-en: Must all the Christian faithful, according to their gifts and ministries, cooperate harmoniously in the Gospel for the building up of the Church?
ag-29-en: Since proclaiming the Gospel to the whole world falls primarily on the bishops, should one competent office direct and coordinate all missions and missionary activity?
ag-30-en: Is it the bishop's role, as ruler and center of diocesan unity, to promote, direct, and coordinate missionary activity while preserving the zeal of those who share the work?
ag-31-en: Should episcopal conferences take common counsel on weightier missionary questions and pool resources for shared projects such as seminaries and pastoral centers?
ag-32-en: Should ecclesiastical institutes and associations coordinate their activities and defer to the local Ordinary in all that concerns missionary activity itself?
ag-33-en: Should institutes engaged in missionary activity in the same territory coordinate their work through conferences of Religious in close touch with episcopal conferences?
ag-34-en: Does right missionary activity require scientific preparation, especially for dialogue with non-Christian religions and cultures, and generous collaboration from missiological institutes?
ag-35-en: Since the whole Church is missionary and evangelization is a basic duty of the People of God, are all invited to interior renewal so as to share in missionary work among the nations?
ag-36-en: Are all the faithful, incorporated into Christ by baptism, confirmation, and the Eucharist, duty-bound to cooperate in the expansion of His Body and the work of evangelization?
ag-37-en: Must dioceses and parishes witness Christ before the nations by extending their charity to the ends of the earth as carefully as to their own members?
ag-38-en: Are all bishops, as members of the apostolic college with and under Peter, consecrated not only for one diocese but for the salvation of the entire world?
ag-39-en: Do priests, personally representing Christ and collaborating with bishops, have a life consecrated also to the service of the missions?
ag-40-en: Have contemplative and active religious institutes a principal role in the evangelization of the world, bound by charity to a truly catholic spirit?
ag-41-en: Do laymen cooperate in the Church's evangelizing mission as witnesses and living instruments, especially when called by God and accepted by the bishop for this work?
ag-42-en: Do the council Fathers with the Roman Pontiff salute the heralds of the Gospel, especially those persecuted for Christ, and pray that God's Kingdom may come on earth?
cd-1-en: Did Christ the Lord come to save His people from their sins and sanctify all, sending His Apostles as He Himself was sent by the Father?
cd-2-en: Does the Roman pontiff, as successor of Peter, enjoy by divine institution supreme, full, immediate, and universal authority over the care of souls?
cd-3-en: Do bishops, having received their office through episcopal consecration, exercise it in communion with and under the authority of the supreme pontiff?
cd-4-en: By sacramental consecration and hierarchical communion, are bishops members of the episcopal college which, with its head the Roman pontiff, holds supreme power over the universal Church?
cd-5-en: Do bishops chosen from various parts of the world assist the supreme pastor in a Synod of Bishops acting in the name of the entire Catholic episcopate?
cd-6-en: As successors of the Apostles and members of the episcopal college, are bishops bound together in concern for all the churches by divine institution?
cd-7-en: Should bishops embrace in brotherly affection those fellow bishops who for Christ's sake suffer slander, poverty, imprisonment, or exclusion from ministry?
cd-8-en: Do diocesan bishops, as successors of the Apostles, have all ordinary, proper, and immediate authority needed for their pastoral office, without infringing the Roman pontiff's power to reserve cases?
cd-9-en: In exercising supreme power in the universal Church, does the Roman pontiff make use of the Roman Curia, which acts in his name and with his authority?
cd-10-en: Should members, officials, and consultors of the Roman Curia, as well as papal legates, be more widely drawn from various regions of the Church?
cd-11-en: Is a diocese a portion of the people of God entrusted to a bishop with the cooperation of the presbytery, constituting a particular church in which the one Church of Christ is truly present?
cd-12-en: In their duty of teaching, should bishops announce the Gospel of Christ, expound the whole mystery of Christ, and call people to faith in the power of the Spirit?
cd-13-en: Should bishops present Christian doctrine adapted to the needs of the times, responding to the difficulties that especially burden people, while guarding and propagating that doctrine?
cd-14-en: Should bishops ensure that catechetical instruction, based on Sacred Scripture, is carefully given to children, adolescents, youths, and adults by methods suited to their circumstances?
cd-15-en: In their office of sanctifying, do bishops enjoy the fullness of the sacrament of orders, with priests and deacons dependent upon them in the exercise of their authority?
cd-16-en: In their office as father and pastor, should bishops stand among their people as those who serve, knowing their sheep as good shepherds and true fathers?
cd-17-en: Should various forms of the apostolate be encouraged and coordinated under the bishop so that catechetical, missionary, charitable, and other pastoral works act in harmony?
cd-18-en: Should special pastoral concern be shown for migrants, exiles, refugees, seafarers, air-travelers, and others who cannot sufficiently use ordinary parish care?
cd-19-en: In discharging their apostolic office for the salvation of souls, do bishops enjoy full freedom and independence from any civil authority?
cd-20-en: Does the right of nominating and appointing bishops belong properly and exclusively to the competent ecclesiastical authority?
cd-21-en: Are diocesan bishops who become less capable of fulfilling their duties because of age or other serious reason earnestly requested to offer their resignation from office?
cd-22-en: For a diocese to fulfill its purpose, must its boundaries and the distribution of clergy and resources be reasonably determined according to the needs of the apostolate?
cd-23-en: In revising diocesan boundaries, must first place be given to the organic unity of each diocese, with due regard to personnel, offices, and institutions?
cd-24-en: Should competent episcopal conferences examine proposed changes of dioceses for their territory and propose their recommendations to the Apostolic See?
cd-25-en: May auxiliary bishops be appointed when the diocesan bishop cannot personally fulfill all his episcopal duties as the good of souls demands?
cd-26-en: When the good of souls demands it, should the diocesan bishop not hesitate to ask for one or more auxiliaries without right of succession, to be appointed as vicars under his authority?
cd-27-en: Is the most important office in the diocesan curia that of vicar general, and may the bishop also name episcopal vicars with like authority for a part of the diocese or a determined task?
cd-28-en: Do all priests, diocesan and religious, participate with the bishop in the one priesthood of Christ, with diocesan priests holding first place in the care of souls of a particular church?
cd-29-en: Are priests charged with supra-parochial pastoral offices or apostolic organizations among the bishop's closer collaborators in the care of souls?
cd-30-en: Are pastors cooperators of the bishop in a very special way, entrusted in their own name with the care of souls in a part of the diocese under his authority?
cd-31-en: In judging a priest's suitability for a parish, should the bishop consider not only doctrine but also piety, apostolic zeal, and the other gifts needed for the care of souls?
cd-32-en: Should concern for souls be the basis for determining or reconsidering the erection, suppression, or other changes of parishes that the bishop may undertake?
cd-33-en: Do all Religious, each according to proper vocation, have the duty of cooperating zealously in building up the Mystical Body of Christ and serving the particular churches?
cd-34-en: Are religious priests by consecration assumed into the responsibilities of the presbyterate as prudent cooperators of the episcopal order in the care of souls?
cd-35-en: Should all Religious look upon bishops as successors of the Apostles with devoted respect, and when legitimately called to the apostolate serve as active and obedient helpers?
cd-36-en: From the Church's earliest centuries, did bishops pool their abilities in synods and councils to teach the faith and order ecclesiastical discipline for the common good?
cd-37-en: Is it supremely fitting that bishops of the same nation or region form an episcopal conference meeting at fixed times for a more fruitful apostolate?
cd-38-en: Is an episcopal conference a council in which the bishops of a nation or territory jointly exercise their pastoral office for the greater good of the Church?
cd-39-en: Does the good of souls require fitting boundaries not only for dioceses but also for ecclesiastical provinces, and sometimes the establishment of new ecclesiastical regions?
cd-40-en: Does this sacred synod decree the following measures in order to accomplish its aims for ecclesiastical provinces and regions?
cd-41-en: Should competent episcopal conferences examine the boundaries of provinces and the establishment of regions and submit their suggestions to the Apostolic See?
cd-42-en: When pastoral needs require joint undertakings, is it fitting that certain offices serving many dioceses be created, possibly filled by bishops, in fraternal cooperation with diocesan bishops?
cd-43-en: Because of the unique conditions of military life, should a military vicariate be established in every nation if possible, with bishops releasing suitable priests as chaplains?
cd-44-en: Does the sacred synod prescribe that in revising the code of canon law suitable laws be drawn up in keeping with the principles of this decree?
dh-1-en: Has contemporary awareness of human dignity increased the demand that people act on their own judgment in responsible freedom, and that constitutional limits restrain governmental power?
dh-2-en: Does the human person have a right to religious freedom, meaning immunity from coercion so that no one is forced to act against his own beliefs, privately or publicly, within due limits?
dh-3-en: Is the highest norm of human life the divine law—eternal, objective, and universal—so that every person has the duty and therefore the right to seek the truth?
dh-4-en: Is immunity from coercion in religious matters also to be recognized when people act in community, so that religious communities may govern themselves and worship publicly within just public order?
dh-5-en: Does the family have the right to live its domestic religious life under parental guidance, and do parents have the right to determine their children's religious education?
dh-6-en: Since the common welfare chiefly consists in protecting rights and performing duties, does care for the right to religious freedom devolve upon citizens, social groups, government, and the Church?
dh-7-en: Is the exercise of religious freedom in society subject to regulatory norms of personal and social responsibility, respect for others' rights, and the common welfare?
dh-8-en: Should educators form people who both respect the moral order and obey lawful authority, and yet act on their own judgment rather than lose responsible freedom under social pressures?
dh-9-en: Does the doctrine of religious freedom have its foundation in the dignity of the person and also roots in divine revelation, so that Christians are bound to respect it conscientiously?
dh-10-en: Is it a major tenet of Catholic doctrine that man's response to God in faith must be free, so that no one is to be forced to embrace the Christian faith against his own will?
dh-11-en: Does God call people to serve Him in spirit and in truth so that they are bound in conscience yet stand under no compulsion, to be guided by their own judgment in freedom?
dh-12-en: In faithfulness to the Gospel, does the Church follow Christ and the apostles when she recognizes and supports the principle of religious freedom as befitting human dignity and divine revelation?
dh-13-en: Is it preeminent for the good of the Church and society that the Church enjoy that full measure of freedom which her care for the salvation of people requires?
dh-14-en: To be faithful to the command to teach all nations, must the Catholic Church work urgently that the word of God be spread abroad and glorified?
dh-15-en: Do people today rightly want freely to profess their religion in private and in public, and should religious freedom as a civil right be honored wherever governments still hinder it?
dv-1-en: Following Trent and Vatican I, does this council wish to set forth authentic doctrine on divine revelation and how it is handed on, so that by hearing the message of salvation the whole world may believe?
dv-2-en: Did God in His goodness and wisdom choose to reveal Himself and make known the hidden purpose of His will, so that through Christ people might have access to the Father in the Holy Spirit?
dv-3-en: Does God give an enduring witness to Himself in created realities, and from the start manifest Himself further in the history of salvation after the fall of our first parents?
dv-4-en: After speaking through the prophets, has God now spoken to us in His Son, the Word made flesh, who completes the work of salvation given Him by the Father?
dv-5-en: Is the obedience of faith to be given to God who reveals, an obedience by which a person freely commits the whole self to God, assisted by grace and the interior help of the Holy Spirit?
dv-6-en: Through divine revelation, did God choose to show forth and communicate Himself and His eternal decisions regarding salvation, sharing treasures that transcend human understanding?
dv-7-en: Has God seen to it that what He revealed for the salvation of all nations would abide perpetually in its full integrity and be handed on to all generations through the Apostles?
dv-8-en: Was apostolic preaching, expressed especially in the inspired books, to be preserved by an unending succession of preachers until the end of time?
dv-9-en: Is there a close connection between sacred tradition and Sacred Scripture, both flowing from the same divine wellspring and tending toward the same end?
dv-10-en: Do sacred tradition and Sacred Scripture form one sacred deposit of the word of God committed to the Church, whose authentic interpretation is entrusted to the living teaching office?
dv-11-en: Are the books of both the Old and New Testaments in their entirety sacred and canonical because, written under the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, they have God as their author?
dv-12-en: Since God speaks in Scripture through men in human fashion, should interpreters carefully investigate what the sacred writers really intended and what God wanted to manifest by their words?
dv-13-en: In Sacred Scripture, while God's truth and holiness remain intact, are the words of God expressed in human language by a marvelous condescension adapted to our weak human nature?
dv-14-en: In preparing the salvation of the human race, did God choose a people, enter into covenant with Abraham and Israel, and so manifest Himself as the one true and living God?
dv-15-en: Was the principal purpose of the old covenant to prepare for the coming of Christ and the messianic kingdom, announcing that coming by prophecy and indicating its meaning through types?
dv-16-en: Did God wisely arrange that the New Testament be hidden in the Old and the Old be made manifest in the New, so that the Old Testament books acquire their full meaning in the New?
dv-17-en: Is the word of God set forth in a most excellent way in the New Testament writings, in which the Word made flesh established God's kingdom and completed His work by death, resurrection, and Ascension?
dv-18-en: Among all the Scriptures, do the four Gospels have special preeminence as the principal witness to the life and teaching of the incarnate Word, and are they of apostolic origin?
dv-19-en: Does the Church firmly hold that the four Gospels, whose historical character she asserts, faithfully hand on what Jesus really did and taught for eternal salvation?
dv-20-en: Besides the four Gospels, does the New Testament canon also contain the epistles of Paul and other apostolic writings that confirm Christ's teaching and recount the Church's beginnings?
dv-21-en: Has the Church always venerated the divine Scriptures as she venerates the body of the Lord, maintaining them together with sacred tradition as the supreme rule of faith?
dv-22-en: Should easy access to Sacred Scripture be provided for all the Christian faithful through suitable and correct translations authorized by the Church?
dv-23-en: Should Catholic exegetes and other students of sacred theology, under the Church's teaching office, devote their energies to a deeper understanding of the Sacred Scriptures?
dv-24-en: Does sacred theology rest on the written word of God together with sacred tradition as its primary foundation, so that study of the sacred page is as it were the soul of sacred theology?
dv-25-en: Must all the clergy hold fast to the Sacred Scriptures through diligent reading and careful study so as to share the abundant wealth of the divine word with the faithful?
dv-26-en: Through reading and study of the sacred books, may the word of God spread rapidly and be glorified, filling hearts with the treasure of revelation entrusted to the Church?
ge-1-en: Do all people of every race, condition, and age have an inalienable right to an education keeping with their ultimate goal, ability, and culture, and aimed at true human formation?
ge-2-en: Since Christians have become children of God by water and the Holy Spirit, do they have a right to a Christian education that leads them into the mystery of salvation and the gift of Faith?
ge-3-en: Since parents have given children life, are they bound by the most serious obligation to educate them and must they be recognized as the primary and principal educators?
ge-4-en: In fulfilling her educational role, is the Church especially concerned with catechetical instruction, which enlightens faith and leads to intelligent participation in the liturgical mystery?
ge-5-en: Among educational instruments, does the school have special importance for developing intellectual faculties, forming right judgment, handing on culture, and preparing for professional life?
ge-6-en: Must parents who have the primary right and duty to educate their children enjoy true liberty in choosing schools, with public subsidies protecting that freedom of conscience?
ge-7-en: Must the Church care for the moral and religious education of her children trained in non-Catholic schools, especially through priests and laymen who teach the doctrine of salvation?
ge-8-en: Is the proper function of the Catholic school to create a community atmosphere animated by the Gospel spirit of freedom and charity and to order human culture to the news of salvation?
ge-9-en: Must all schools dependent on the Church conform as far as possible to the concept of a Catholic school, taking different forms according to local circumstances?
ge-10-en: In Catholic colleges and universities, should individual subjects be pursued according to their own principles and liberty of scientific inquiry toward ever deeper understanding?
ge-11-en: Do faculties of the sacred sciences bear responsibility for preparing students for priestly ministry, teaching, and a more rigorous intellectual apostolate?
ge-12-en: Is suitable cooperation among Catholic schools, and between these and other schools, altogether necessary for the good of all mankind?
gs-1-en: Are the joys and hopes, griefs and anxieties of the people of this age, especially the poor and afflicted, also the joys and hopes, griefs and anxieties of the followers of Christ?
gs-2-en: Does this council address itself not only to the sons of the Church and all who invoke Christ's name, but to the whole of humanity, explaining the Church's presence in today's world?
gs-3-en: Can this council, giving witness to the faith of the whole people of God, provide eloquent proof of its solidarity with, respect for, and love of the entire human family?
gs-4-en: Has the Church always had the duty of scrutinizing the signs of the times and interpreting them in the light of the Gospel, responding to perennial questions about this life and the life to come?
gs-5-en: Do today's spiritual agitation and changing conditions of life form part of a broader revolution in which science and technology increasingly transform culture and the face of the earth?
gs-6-en: Are traditional local communities such as families, clans, and villages experiencing thorough change as industrial society spreads and city living multiplies?
gs-7-en: Do rapid changes in attitudes and human structures frequently call accepted values into question, especially among young people impatient to take part in society?
gs-8-en: Does rapid and often disorderly development, together with keener awareness of inequalities, beget or intensify contradictions and imbalances within persons and societies?
gs-9-en: Is there a growing conviction that humanity should establish a political, social, and economic order that serves people and helps them affirm the dignity proper to them?
gs-10-en: Are the imbalances of the modern world linked with a more basic imbalance rooted in the heart of man, who as a weak and sinful being often does what he would not?
gs-11-en: Does the People of God, led by the Lord's Spirit, labor to decipher authentic signs of God's presence and purpose in the happenings, needs, and desires of our age?
gs-12-en: Although all things on earth should be related to man as their center and crown, does the Church, endowed with light from God, offer solutions so that man's true nature may be understood?
gs-13-en: Although made by God in holiness, did man from the onset of history abuse his liberty, set himself against God, and find in his heart inclinations toward evil?
gs-14-en: Though made of body and soul, is man one, so that he may not despise his bodily life but must regard his body as good and honorable since God created it and will raise it up?
gs-15-en: By his intellect, does man surpass the material universe and share in the light of the divine mind, able to search beyond observable data for more penetrating truths?
gs-16-en: In the depths of conscience, does man detect a law written by God which he does not impose upon himself, so that to obey it is the very dignity of man?
gs-17-en: Is authentic freedom an exceptional sign of the divine image within man, so that only in freedom can he direct himself toward goodness and seek his Creator spontaneously?
gs-18-en: In the face of death, does man rightly abhor utter ruin and perpetual extinction because he bears in himself an eternal seed which cannot be reduced to sheer matter?
gs-19-en: Does the root reason for human dignity lie in man's call to communion with God, so that he cannot live fully according to truth unless he freely acknowledges God's love?
gs-20-en: Does modern systematic atheism stretch the desire for human independence so far that it poses difficulties against any dependence on God as author and purpose of all things?
gs-21-en: Has the Church repudiated doctrines and actions that contradict reason and common experience and dethrone man, while still seeking to examine seriously the questions atheism raises?
gs-22-en: Is it only in the mystery of the incarnate Word that the mystery of man takes on light, since Christ the final Adam fully reveals man to himself and makes his supreme calling clear?
gs-23-en: Does brotherly dialogue among people reach its perfection not merely on the level of technical progress, but on the deeper level of interpersonal relationships that respect spiritual dignity?
gs-24-en: Has God willed that all people constitute one family and treat one another in a spirit of brotherhood, so that love of God cannot be separated from love of neighbor?
gs-25-en: Does man's social nature make evident that the progress of the human person and the advance of society hinge on one another, with the human person as the beginning and goal of social institutions?
gs-26-en: As human interdependence spreads worldwide, does the common good take on an increasingly universal complexion involving rights and duties with respect to the whole human race?
gs-27-en: Must everyone consider every neighbor without exception as another self, taking into account first of all life and the means necessary to living it with dignity?
gs-28-en: Should respect and love be extended also to those who think or act differently in social, political, and even religious matters, without becoming indifferent to truth and goodness?
gs-29-en: Since all possess a rational soul, are created in God's likeness, and enjoy the same divine calling, must the basic equality of all receive increasingly greater recognition against every discrimination?
gs-30-en: Do the obligations of justice and love require that each person contribute to the common good and assist the institutions dedicated to bettering the conditions of human life?
gs-31-en: Must people be carefully educated to a higher degree of culture, especially the youth of every social background, so that great-souled persons required by our times may be formed?
gs-32-en: As God did not create man for life in isolation, has it pleased God to make people holy and save them not merely as individuals but by making them into a single people?
gs-33-en: Through science and technology, has man extended his mastery over nearly the whole of nature, while a human family gradually recognizes itself as a single world community?
gs-34-en: Does human activity to better the circumstances of life, considered in itself, accord with God's will, since man created in God's image received a mandate to subject the earth to himself?
gs-35-en: When a person works, does he not only alter things and society but also develop himself, so that a person is more precious for what he is than for what he has?
gs-36-en: If by autonomy of earthly affairs we mean that created things and societies enjoy their own laws and values to be deciphered and regulated by people, is that autonomy entirely right and in harmony with the Creator's will?
gs-37-en: While human progress is a great advantage, does it also bring a strong temptation whereby the order of values is jumbled and individuals heed only their own interests?
gs-38-en: Did God's Word, made flesh, reveal that God is love and teach that the new command of love is the basic law of human perfection and of the world's transformation?
gs-39-en: Are we taught that God is preparing a new dwelling place and a new earth where justice will abide, while the shape of this world deformed by sin will pass away?
gs-40-en: Do the dignity of the human person, the human community, and the meaning of human activity lay the foundation for the relationship and dialogue between the Church and the world?
gs-41-en: Since the Church is entrusted with revealing the mystery of God as man's ultimate goal, does she at the same time open up to man the innermost truth about his own existence?
gs-42-en: Did Christ give His Church no proper mission in the political, economic, or social order, yet from her religious mission come a light and energy that can structure the human community according to divine law?
gs-43-en: Must Christians, as citizens of two cities, discharge their earthly duties conscientiously in a Gospel spirit, neither shirking them nor treating religion as irrelevant to them?
gs-44-en: Does the Church herself know how richly she has profited by human history, the progress of the sciences, and the treasures of various cultures, which open new roads to truth?
gs-45-en: While helping the world and receiving benefits from it, does the Church have a single intention: that God's kingdom may come and that the salvation of the whole human race may come to pass?
gs-46-en: Having set forth the dignity of the person and human work in the world, does the council now direct attention to particularly urgent needs of the present age in the light of the Gospel?
gs-47-en: Is the well-being of the individual person and of human and Christian society intimately linked with the healthy condition of the community produced by marriage and family?
gs-48-en: Has the intimate partnership of married life and love been established by the Creator and rooted in the irrevocable personal consent of the spouses, so that the sacred bond no longer depends on human decisions alone?
gs-49-en: Is true conjugal love an eminently human love directed from one person to another through an affection of the will, involving the good of the whole person?
gs-50-en: Are marriage and conjugal love by their nature ordained toward the begetting and educating of children, who are the supreme gift of marriage?
gs-51-en: When modern conditions keep couples from increasing their families for a time, must the faithful exercise of conjugal love and the full intimacy of married life still be carefully safeguarded?
gs-52-en: Is the family a kind of school of deeper humanity that needs communion of minds between spouses and the painstaking cooperation of parents in educating their children?
gs-53-en: Does man come to a true and full humanity only through culture, that is, through the cultivation of the goods and values of nature?
gs-54-en: Have the circumstances of modern life been so profoundly changed socially and culturally that we can speak of a new age of human history open to the further extension of culture?
gs-55-en: Is there throughout the world a mounting sense that men and women themselves are the authors and artisans of their community's culture, with growing autonomy and responsibility?
gs-56-en: As people sense responsibility for cultural progress, must they also face anxious questions about how increased exchanges among cultures can remain fruitful without destroying each people's proper character?
gs-57-en: Does the Christian duty to seek the things that are above in no way decrease, but rather increase, the obligation to work with all people in building a more human world?
